question: get_flow
answer:
1. `httpx.get(url, ...)` calls the module-level `request("GET", url, ...)`. That helper creates a synchronous `Client` in a context manager and calls `client.request(...)`. [httpx/_api.py](httpx/_api.py#L174) · [httpx/_api.py](httpx/_api.py#L38)
2. `Client.request()` calls `BaseClient.build_request()`, which merges client defaults, sets timeout metadata, and constructs a `Request`. It then passes the request to `Client.send()`. [httpx/_client.py](httpx/_client.py#L771) · [httpx/_client.py](httpx/_client.py#L340) · [httpx/_models.py](httpx/_models.py#L382)
3. `Client.send()` resolves authentication and calls `_send_handling_auth()`. That method starts `auth.sync_auth_flow(request)` and passes the yielded request to `_send_handling_redirects()`, which runs any request hooks before calling `_send_single_request()`. [httpx/_client.py](httpx/_client.py#L879) · [httpx/_client.py](httpx/_client.py#L930) · [httpx/_client.py](httpx/_client.py#L964)
4. `_send_single_request()` calls `_transport_for_url(request.url)` to select the default `HTTPTransport` or a matching proxy transport. The request reaches the transport at `transport.handle_request(request)`. [httpx/_client.py](httpx/_client.py#L1001) · [httpx/_client.py](httpx/_client.py#L760)
